title: Regional fleet headroom vs precision tradeoff - capacity sheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick-reference capacity planning sheet that maps per-GPU throughput (tokens/s), end-to-end p95 latency, and estimated quality delta for common quantization and batching configurations. Used by infra planning and capacity sales to size regional fleets and set headroom targets for peak SLAs.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline model: rw-7b-chat-v2 (FP16 reference)
- Token distribution: mean request length = 60 tokens, tail 95th = 320 tokens
- Target SLA: p95 <= 300 ms for interactive tier (small prompt + single-shot generation)
- Measurement hardware: A100 80GB equivalent (baseline perf), G4-like fleet not considered here
- Observed quality baseline (FP16) = 0% delta (anchor).

Summary table (per-GPU numbers):
Columns: quant_level | batch_size | tokens/sec/gpu | p95_lat_ms (60t) | p95_lat_ms (320t) | est_quality_delta_vs_fp16
FP16 | 1 | 1200 | 45 | 230 | 0.0%
FP16 | 8 | 7200 | 120 | 610 | 0.0%
INT8 | 1 | 1650 | 38 | 195 | -0.9% (semantic fidelity)
INT8 | 8 | 9800 | 95 | 520 | -1.8%
4-bit | 1 | 2100 | 34 | 170 | -3.6%
4-bit | 8 | 12600 | 82 | 420 | -7.2%

Interpretation notes:
- Single-request latency (batch_size=1) dominates interactive experiences; quantization gains here are modest but meaningful for p95 at long sequences because of KV cache memory pressure reductions.
- High batch sizes increase tokens/sec dramatically but push p95 latency above interactive SLA for long sequences. Use batched routing only for background/generation jobs.
- Quality delta is estimated from internal evals on open-source chat prompts and human spot checks — relative quality loss grows nonlinearly when combining aggressive quant (4-bit) with large effective batch sizes.

Regional capacity headroom scenarios (current steady-state traffic -> projected peak 2x during sales events):
Table columns: region | current_gpu_pool | util_now_avg | safe_headroom_pct | recommended_additional_gpus (to maintain p95<=300ms at 2x) | notes
us-west1 | 120 | 72% | 25% | +24 | prioritize INT8 rollout for interactive tier to avoid full add; test canary in us-west1-a
us-east1 | 200 | 64% | 30% | +40 | prefer mixed fleet (FP16 + 4-bit overflow) on dedicated nodes, reserve burst capacity in us-east2
eu-west1 | 80 | 78% | 30% | +24 | EU regulator customers prefer FP16 for auditability — limit 4-bit to non-sensitive workloads
apac-sg1 | 40 | 55% | 40% | +16 | small pool; prefer reserved burst from cloud partner vs buying more baseline GPUs

Operational playbook (short):
1) Canary policy: deploy INT8 model variant to 5% of interactive traffic in a single AZ for 48h, monitor p95, regression, and top-k hallucination metric.
2) If p95 improves and quality delta within threshold (<-2%), expand to 25% and enable autoscale policy with target_util=65%.
3) For sales-event surge: shift candidate background traffic to batched INT8 / 4-bit nodes and pinch interactive traffic to FP16/INT8 pool with headroom target 25%.
4) Fallback: if quality alerts (>3% regression) trigger, automatic fallback to FP16 model variant with traffic re-route to dedicated FP16 nodes in same region.

Sizing calc (worked example — us-west1):
- Peak expected QPS (token-aware): 2,400 concurrent small-interactive sessions -> avg token/s demand = 2,400 * 60 = 144k tokens/s.
- Preferred config for interactive: INT8 batch=1 => 1650 tokens/s/gpu.
- GPUs required = ceil(144k / 1650) = 88 GPUs to meet demand.
- Current pool 120 GPUs at 72% util -> effective available = 120 * 1650 * (1 - 0.72) = 55440 tokens/s spare (not a direct mapping but used to approximate headroom).
- To guarantee p95<=300ms at 2x peak, add +24 GPUs (recommended).

Risk register / open questions: 
- Model drift: repeated evals required — current delta estimates are from a limited prompt set (JIRA-INFRA-8721).
- Cache behavior: some models show worse p95 at long sequences under 4-bit due to KV cache alignment; need microbenchmarks on sequence lengths >1024 (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pr/4567).
- Regional procurement lead times: GCP capacity guarantees vs vendor spot availability differ by region — buying ahead might be cheaper than burst allocation.

Action items: 
- Dmitri: run long-sequence KV cache microbench across quant levels (due 2026-03-10).
- Anika: set up canary INT8 rollout in us-west1-a and add observability tags for quality regression alerts (due 2026-03-08).
- Chris: update sales/finance sizing template with these per-GPU tokens/s numbers and headroom guidance (due 2026-03-12).

Appendix: quick reference performance knobs (for SRE/Oncall):
- target_util for autoscale: 60-70% for mixed-quant fleets (prefer lower for 4-bit heavy nodes)
- burst_policy: prefer cross-AZ burst within same region before inter-region fallback to minimize latency increase
- fallback_thresholds: quality-regression > 2.5% OR p95 increase > 20% triggers rollback to safer model variant

Notes on provenance: derived from internal perf runs (Jan 2026) on baseline A100-equivalent machines, human eval spot checks, and infra sizing heuristics. This sheet is intentionally compact — refer to Confluence page CONFLUENCE-INFRA-quant-batch-notes-2026 for full experiment logs and raw CSVs.
